name: Lake Teletskoye
full: Lake Teletskoye (Altai: Altyn-Kol — “Golden Lake”), northeast of the Altai Republic
near: North: Artybash village and Iogach village (at the source of the Biya); east shore: Yaylyu settlement (reserve headquarters); south: Balykcha village and the Kyrsay tract (mouth of the Chulyshman)
short: The largest and deepest lake in Altai: 78 km long, up to 325 m deep, stretched in an “L” shape through the taiga; on the east shore the Altai Nature Reserve and waterfalls, in the south the mouth of the Chulyshman.
desc: Lake Teletskoye lies at 434 m and stretches roughly 78–79 km with a width of up to 5.5 km; its area is about 223 km², and its maximum depth is 323–325 m (one of the deepest lakes in Russia and the world). According to different sources, anywhere from 19 large to more than 70 rivers and streams flow into the lake, the main tributary being the Chulyshman (about 70% of the inflow), and one river flows out — the Biya. The local name is Altyn-Kol (“Golden Lake”); the Russian name “Teletskoye” was given about 400 years ago after the Teleuts who lived on its shores. The water is cold: in the north in summer about +10…+12 °C, in the southern part up to +17…+22 °C (other sources say the water rarely warms above +16 °C); the south of the lake is 4–5 °C warmer than the north. The latitudinal (northern) part freezes in winter, while the deep meridional part only once every 7–12 years. The lake is known for sharp winds (nizovka/verkhovka) that quickly raise waves. The whole east shore and the southern part are in the Altai State Nature Biosphere Reserve (part of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”). The north shore is the tourist side: the villages of Artybash and Iogach with dozens of recreation bases, boat piers, a ferry to the south, and the Teletskiy ski resort on Mount Kokuya. The main sights on the water are the Korbu, Kishte, Estyuba and Choodor waterfalls, Kamenny Bay (Stone Bay), Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman, where the road into the valley to Uchar and the Stone Mushrooms begins.
guide: The best part is seeing the lake from the water: take a motorboat at least to Korbu, or better the full-day “Golden Ring” to the south shore. Don't trust a calm: the nizovka wind arrives within half an hour, so bring a warm jacket even in the heat. Altaians call the lake Altyn-Kol, and there is a legend about a year of famine when a rich man threw a gold ingot into the water — hence the “Golden Lake”. For a panorama, ride the lift up Kokuya or hike up Tilan-Tuu (Wolf's Head) above Artybash. And be sure to try smoked Teletskoye whitefish or grayling.
see: The source of the Biya and the bridge in Iogach/Artybash; Mount Kokuya (1385 m, lift) and the Tilan-Tuu viewpoint (740 m); the Korbu, Kishte, Estyuba, Choodor and Ayu-Kechpes waterfalls (from a boat); Kamenny Bay (Stone Bay); Yaylyu settlement — the reserve headquarters; Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman in the south; the Tayozhny zoo in Artybash; the Ortosh ethnographic museum near Kebezen
skip: you aren't up for a long road (160 km from Gorno-Altaysk on a narrow road) and cold water for swimming, and boats and waterfalls don't appeal to you; at the end of the 2026 season, moreover, all the reserve's trails are closed because of bears
diff: Easy (north, boat excursions); moderate to high for a trip to the south shore overland via Katu-Yaryk
when: July–September (warm, boats run and the reserve's trails are open May–September); September — quieter and golden autumn; winter — ice, skiing, almost no frosts
hours: The lake — around the clock, free access; the reserve's eco-educational routes are usually open May–September; in 2026 all the reserve's routes have been closed from late August to the end of the season
daytime: Morning — calm and mirror-like water, boats leave at 7–9 am; sunset — from Tilan-Tuu or Kokuya
how: North (Artybash/Iogach): Barnaul → Gorno-Altaysk 257 km (3.5–4 h), Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash ≈159–160 km (2–3 h by car) along the Teletskoye Trakt via Choya, Turochak/Kebezen; from Novosibirsk to Gorno-Altaysk ≈430 km (5–6 h). Buses from Gorno-Altaysk (≈4 h), Biysk and Barnaul. South (Balykcha/Kyrsay): car ferry from Artybash (5–6 h) or overland: Chuysky Trakt to Aktash → Ulagan road → Ulagan → Balyktuyul → Katu-Yaryk Pass → down the Chulyshman valley to the lake (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass + ≈75 km along the valley), only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV.
needcar: To the north shore — bus or car; on the lake — motorboat; to the south — ferry, motorboat or 4×4 / SUV
self: Yes: to the north by bus or car, with boats and excursions bought on the spot; to the south independently — by ferry with your car or in a 4×4 / SUV via Katu-Yaryk
roadtype: To Artybash — paved road (a narrow two-lane road without shoulders); beyond Artybash along the west shore — dirt road; to the south overland — the Ulagan road (partly paved, then dirt), Katu-Yaryk Pass — a steep gravel serpentine
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash 2.5–3 h by car, ≈4 h by bus; Barnaul → Artybash ≈6–7 h; Novosibirsk → Artybash ≈8–9 h; ferry Artybash → south 5–6 h
stay: Dozens of bases in Artybash and Iogach: from 700 ₽/night (simple tourist bases, mirturbaz) and 2200 ₽ (the Teletskoye Zolotoye eco-hotel) to 15,000–46,000 ₽ (Urochishche Aktra, Altay Village Teletskoe); Altay Time cabins 5000 ₽ (2 people) — 15,000 ₽ (6 people); in the south — campsites and the Vyshe Gor glamping in Balykcha from 2200 ₽
net: A stable mobile signal exists only in Artybash and Iogach (YouTravel, 2026); on the water and on the east shore — patchy; in the Chulyshman valley a signal has appeared but is unstable (T—Zh, 2025); specific operators — to be checked
entry: The lake itself is free. Altai Nature Reserve trails (Korbu, Uchar, Yaylyu): 250 ₽/person (2025); from 31.08.2026 all routes are closed until the end of the season. There is no resort tax in the Altai Republic (under discussion); a tourist tax has been introduced only in the city of Gorno-Altaysk (2025–2026). Separate eco fees for private/local stops at waterfalls — 50–150 ₽ (KP, 2026); tour operators quote ≈750 ₽ for three waterfalls (Sputnik8, 2026). Free, per Turister, for children under 14 and school groups (to be confirmed).
transfer: Taxi Gorno-Altaysk → Artybash ≈3000–4000 ₽ (2020–2023); car ferry to the south 15–17k ₽ (2026); private motorboat to the south ≈78,000 ₽ for 6 h (Extraguide)
bring: A warm waterproof jacket even in summer (nizovka wind), repellent and tick protection, cash (signal and card terminals are not everywhere), sun protection, shoes for wet rocks
warn: On 19.08.2026 a bear fatally attacked a tourist in a tent near Artybash; a curfew was imposed in Artybash and Yaylyu, and all the reserve's routes are closed until the end of the 2026 season — don't pitch a tent in the forest, store food airtight. Ticks (May–July). Sharp winds and waves — don't go out on the water in a boat without experience. The water is cold — dangerous for long swimming. The road to Artybash is narrow, without shoulders.
food: Smoked and fried Teletskoye whitefish, grayling; cedar coffee and herbal tea (a cafe on the Korbu trail); the TsUP cafe at the foot of Kokuya and MKS at the first lift platform; tasting at the Ortosh ethnographic museum
reviews: 2GIS: Lake Teletskoye — 4.6 (173 ratings). Excursions: “Legends of the Golden Lake” 4.9 (151 reviews, Sputnik8), “5 waterfalls and Tilan-Tuu” 4.8 (17), “Journey to the Stone Mushrooms” 4.6 (27). Pros: views, waterfalls, guides; cons: high prices, crowding in July–August, cancellations due to weather and bears, separate eco fees at waterfalls (up to 750 ₽ for three).

p.sum: The base point is Artybash/Iogach on the north shore (≈160 km from Gorno-Altaysk on paved road, bus ≈4 h). You see the lake from a boat: from a 1-hour trip to Estyuba (≈2000 ₽) to the “Golden Ring” to the south (6000–7500 ₽). You can reach the south by car ferry from Artybash (5–6 h, with a car 15–17k ₽) or overland via Ulagan and Katu-Yaryk Pass — only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV. Lodging from 700 ₽ to 46,000 ₽ per night. At the end of the 2026 season the reserve's trails are closed because of bears.

p.season: May–September for boats and trails; July–August is the peak (book lodging in advance); the ferry runs May to early October; winter — skiing on Kokuya, boats don't run.
p.permits: No border-zone permit needed (Turochak district). Visiting the reserve's trails requires a route ticket (250 ₽, 2025) and registration on the route; organized groups need to apply to the reserve. Small boats need the reserve's seasonal permit. In 2026 the trails have been closed since 31.08. Since spring 2025 the reserve has issued permits for private small boats to sail on Lake Teletskoye to the eco trails: points in Artybash (Teletskaya St. 12) and Yaylyu (Tsentralnaya St. 14); you need a passport, a boat ticket and a boat operator's license; tel. +7 (388-22) 2-14-19, agpzmain@mail.ru (Altapress, 2025). Hiking groups register with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) online (forms.mchs.gov.ru/registration_tourist_groups); applications are processed within a day.
p.access: With children — yes (motorboats, Korbu, the lift; children under 5 free on boats). For older people — boat trips and Kokuya. The Korbu trail is not adapted for people with limited mobility. Dogs in the reserve — not found (to be confirmed).
